questions.subject: 英语
questions.question:
【共同材料】For years, biologists counted a rare tree frog by walking through wetlands at night and listening for its call. The method worked, but only when trained researchers were available. A new project placed low-cost recorders beside ponds and invited local volunteers to label short sound clips online. Before using the labels, the research team compared a sample with judgments made by frog experts. Volunteers correctly identified the target call in 91 percent of clear recordings, but their accuracy fell sharply when wind or traffic was loud. The team therefore uses volunteer labels to locate likely frog activity, not as final proof. Experts review uncertain clips, and recorders are moved regularly so that one unusually noisy pond does not shape the whole picture.

The project has already revealed calls at two ponds where the frog had not been reported for a decade. Yet project leader Ana Ruiz resists calling this a population recovery. More recordings may simply make the frogs easier to detect. "Finding a call is a reason to look more closely," she says, "not a reason to stop asking questions."

What do experts do in the project?
options: They build roads around every pond.
They review recordings whose labels are uncertain.
They replace all local volunteers at night.
They count only frogs that can be seen.
questions.solution: 第一段明确说明“Experts review uncertain clips”，即专家复核标签不确定的录音，故选B。
questions.title: 公民科学青蛙声学监测·专家职责

Which additional evidence would most strongly support the claim that the frog population is recovering?
options: Volunteers report that labeling clips is enjoyable.
The price of recorders falls over the next year.

questions.subject: 英语
questions.question:
【共同材料】Visitors to museums often spend only a few seconds in front of each object. To test whether labels could slow them down, the Harbor Museum rewrote the labels in one gallery. The old labels listed dates, materials and an expert interpretation. The new ones kept those facts but ended with a question, such as "What detail would you examine if you could turn this bowl over?" During a six-week trial, observers recorded how long visitors stayed. The median viewing time rose from 18 to 31 seconds. More visitors also discussed objects with companions.

The museum's announcement celebrated the result, but curator Malik Chen offered a qualification. The trial gallery contained unusually colorful objects and was less crowded than the rest of the museum. In addition, longer looking does not necessarily mean deeper understanding. Chen supports keeping some question-based labels, while also testing visitors' later recall and comparing several galleries. His position is neither that labels are powerless nor that one clever sentence can transform learning. It is that a small design choice deserves careful testing before it becomes a general rule.

What did the new labels add after presenting factual information?
options: A question inviting visitors to examine the object.
A request for visitors to leave the gallery.
A complete history of the museum building.
A list of objects available for sale.
questions.solution: 第一段说明新标签保留事实信息，并在结尾增加一个引导观察的问题，故选A。

questions.subject: 英语
questions.question:
【共同材料】After a summer storm flooded the community seed library, Lina expected to find only ruined packets. Instead, neighbors arrived carrying jars, paper bags and notebooks. They did not simply ___(1)___ what had been lost; many brought seeds saved by their own families. Lina first tried to sort everything alone, fearing that different names for the same bean would create ___(2)___. An older gardener suggested recording each name rather than choosing one as "correct." That decision ___(3)___ the collection: the notebook began to hold stories of migration, climate and taste as well as planting dates. When a rare tomato failed to grow in the first trial, the group did not ___(4)___ it as useless. They divided the remaining seeds among gardens with different soils. One plant finally produced fruit, reminding Lina that protecting diversity often means ___(5)___ uncertainty instead of demanding an immediate result.

Choose the best word for blank (1).
options: replace
announce
measure
borrow
questions.solution: 洪水毁坏种子包，邻居带来新种子，语境是他们不只是“替换”损失的种子；replace与what had been lost搭配最恰当。
questions.title: 社区种子库完形·补回损失
